technical.lead: Senate cyber S-407 classified FMRB briefing held on schedule
technical.body: The May 15 14:00 EDT Senate Cyber Subcommittee S-407 classified threshold briefing on the Frontier Model Review Board executive order proceeded on schedule, with the eight-witness slate — NIST Director Locascio, the ODNI cyber lead, the NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, a Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative, the CISA Director, the FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Chief, and the DOE and Treasury cyber assistant secretaries — testifying in the classified session ahead of a 16:30 EDT unclassified press follow-on. A Friday-evening unclassified summary memo confirmed the briefing surfaced no objection to the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway or the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window, and that a classified-annex follow-up question set goes to the witnesses with responses due inside ten business days. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology confirmed its parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft is now circulating for markup scheduling, while White House OSTP held that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22.

technical.lead: Cerebras CBRS prints a fourth straight consolidation day
technical.body: Cerebras CBRS closed the second trading week with a fourth consecutive consolidation day, opening at $197.40 (up 0.2 percent from Thursday's $197.10 close), tightening to a $196.30-$199.10 intraday range, and closing at $198.60 (up 0.8 percent), with trailing-five-session turnover crossing $6.1B and the institutional-buyside cumulative net position estimated at 37 percent of float. Bernstein issued a Friday week-close note holding the post-IPO price-target floor at $185 (Market-Perform) and described the four-day consolidation as having retired the single-event re-rating characterization in favor of a structural second-week base; Morgan Stanley reiterated a $192 target with the upside scenario probability lifted to 41 percent, Wells Fargo Securities held Buy at $208, Jefferies reiterated Outperform at $225, and UBS initiated at Neutral with a $205 target. CBRS options traded a 4.1x call-skew (about 71,400 calls versus 17,400 puts), the second-widest print since the IPO debut. The Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close held its late-Q2 2026 window, with the Saudi PIF contingent-secondary discussion narrowing to a 14-21 day execution window.

technical.lead: Eleventh agentic-AI tooling CVE drops — Haystack path traversal
technical.body: An eleventh agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE landed Friday, extending Thursday's Trail of Bits ten-CVE taxonomy. Haystack CVE-2026-45013 (CVSS 8.5) is a path-traversal vulnerability in the pipeline-component manifest fetcher's nested-dependency resolver that lets an attacker overwrite arbitrary host paths during transitive component-manifest resolution, mirroring the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 manifest-fetcher pattern but at the nested-dependency resolution surface; the Haystack maintainer team shipped v2.9.4 same-day with the patch plus a backport advisory for the v2.8.x and v2.7.x branches. Trail of Bits published a Friday addendum updating its taxonomy from ten to eleven agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs, folding a nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization extension into the manifest-allowlist-validation tier. DeepMind, Meta AI, Anthropic, and Microsoft co-published a joint follow-up addendum v4 (arxiv 2605.06712v4) extending the v3 paper with the nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization pattern, and LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, and Pydantic AI reaffirmed that the mid-June default-shipment commitment now covers all four tier-and-sub-tier surfaces plus the nested-dependency-resolution extension.

technical.lead: Claude Code 3.0 registry growth normalizes; 64 gated tenants
technical.body: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 day-eight registry telemetry showed a Friday continuation of second-week growth-rate normalization, with the daily gain holding in the sub-7-percent band. The sandboxed-skill registry counted 26,180 published skills (up from 24,640 Thursday, +6.3 percent — the fifth consecutive sub-15-percent gain and second consecutive sub-7-percent reading), with 2.49M skill installs across the eighth 24 hours and auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills reaching 58. Anthropic's Friday operations summary noted the Mythos-Preview gated-tenant cohort crossed to 64 enterprise customers after Italy's Leonardo Electronics, Germany's Hensoldt Sensors, Norway's Kongsberg Defence Aerospace, and Finland's Patria Land Systems all signed the contractual ethics-and-misuse rider, extending the rider across the Continental European and Nordic allied defense industrial base. Simon Willison's Friday note documented that the open-source verification harness now produces a deterministic per-tenant attestation-log audit trail across all 64 gated tenants, with cross-tenant compositional safety checks completing in under 58 seconds — confirming the Verifiable Per-Tenant Capability Attestation paper's demonstration cycle holds at three-continent multi-tenant scale.

technical.lead: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 hits 72 units; first three-line coordination
technical.body: A Friday Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Fremont operations note reported the first 72 Gen 3 units active on the production line plus the first three-line cross-cell coordination demonstration. Tesla confirmed a sixth cohort of 12 Gen 3 units activated at the Fremont automotive-line cell-pickup-plus-torque-fastening station, bringing the active count to 72 of the disclosed 240-unit allocation (30 percent reached), with cycle-time tightening to a 1.04x human-baseline envelope versus Thursday's 1.06x at the 60-unit milestone. A Friday-morning 360-second clip showed the first three-line cross-cell coordination across the Fremont automotive, sub-assembly, and battery-module lines, with twenty-eight Gen 3 units coordinating a multi-station sealed parts-transfer chain — the first three-line coordination in production. Stellantis confirmed its Detroit 60-unit pilot still activates June 8 and reaffirmed the Auburn Hills 30-unit second-line pilot for fiscal Q3 2026, while Volkswagen Wolfsburg's dual-platform allocation set the Optimus cohort first-activation date as June 22, joining BMW Spartanburg as the second OEM running two humanoid platforms in production at one site.
